idea-plugin.name: Terminal Tab Tailor
idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New ?

Requirement
  • IntelliJ IDEA 2025.3 or later: the API that lets a plugin open the terminal engine you selected only exists from 2025.3. If you are on an earlier version, 1.5.1 remains available and keeps working.
Added
  • Keep the name of the current folder: a new option under Settings > Tools > Terminal Tab Tailor. A tab stops being named once and for all and follows its shell instead - cd ../frontend and the tab becomes frontend. It covers every tab in the Terminal tool window, whatever opened them, on either engine. Renaming a tab yourself takes it back out of the loop, and your date option still applies. Off by default.
  • Parent folders to include: src alone tells you little when every module has one, so ask for 1 and the tab reads TerminalTabTailor/src, for 2 and it reads workspace/TerminalTabTailor/src. It applies to every tab, the name it gets when it opens as much as the one it takes while following its shell. The module and project naming styles are unaffected, being names rather than paths. Defaults to 1.
  • On Windows this works with PowerShell and cmd only. No other shell reports a working directory that follows it: WSL, ssh and docker hide the real shell behind a launcher, while Git Bash, MSYS and Cygwin keep an emulated directory the Windows process never learns about - and the IDE loads no shell integration for any of them. Those tabs simply keep the name they opened with. On macOS and Linux, bash, sh, zsh, fish, dash and ksh are followed too.
Fixed
  • Sorting no longer moves you: re-sorting the tab strip used to hand the selection to a neighbouring tab, drop the keyboard focus so you had to click back into the command line before typing again, and could collapse the Terminal tool window when a single tab was open. All three are gone, which also fixes the same jump when applying the settings. Focus only returns to a terminal that already had it, so a tab renaming itself never pulls you out of the editor.
idea-plugin.description:
Terminal Tab Tailor significantly enhances the IntelliJ IDEA workflow by dynamically renaming terminal tabs to reflect the currently selected item in your project tree. This feature greatly aids in organizing your workspace and navigating effortlessly between numerous terminal sessions.

Simply select a file or folder within your project tree and initiate a terminal session from that context.

Pro-tip: Ctrl+Shift+X opens a terminal for the current selection right away. Rebind it under Settings > Keymap if it clashes with your own shortcuts.

Three ways to open a tailored tab
  • Open In > Terminal - Terminal Tab Tailor takes over the IDE's own "open in terminal" entries, offering Terminal (Reworked) and Terminal (Classic) so you pick the engine on the spot. Every place you already open a terminal from produces a tailored tab.
  • The TTT Button - the "Open in Terminal" action in one click, from the terminal toolbar, using your most recent selection.
  • Rename Session - right-click any tab to name it yourself. Your sort order is re-applied straight away and the renamed tab stays selected.
Choose what the TTT Button follows:
  • Use the last selection from the Project Tree.
  • Use the last selected Tab from the File Editor.
  • Use the most recent selection, whether from the Project Tree or the File Editor Manager.
  • Use the project name, always.
Options & Sort
  • Reuse an existing tab when the names match.
  • Prompt the renaming dialogue each time a new terminal tab is opened.
  • Keep the name of the current folder - tabs follow their shell, so a cd renames the tab. On Windows this works with PowerShell and cmd only. Renaming a tab yourself takes it back out of the loop.
  • Add parent folders to a tab's name, so it reads TerminalTabTailor/src rather than src.
  • Incorporate the current date into tab names (with a customizable pattern, defaulting to dd-MM-yy).
  • Maintain tabs in perpetual alphabetical order.
  • Maintain tabs sorted by descending date.
  • Do not sort tabs.
Whichever you choose, opening or reusing a tab brings the terminal window to the front and selects that tab.

Choose from a variety of naming conventions to suit your workflow:
  • Permit the use of file names directly.
  • Default to directory names, utilizing the parent directory's name for files.
  • Adopt the name of the parent module.
  • Use the parent module's directory name for a more structured approach.
  • Consistently use the project's name for all terminal tabs.
Configurability is at the heart of Terminal Tab Tailor. Find the settings in Settings > Tools > Terminal Tab Tailor, or via Terminal Tab Tailor Settings in the dropdown next to + in the Terminal tool window.
